title: Vow and Postcard
premise: Elodie Halloran has built a careful life ghostwriting other people's truths, including the memoir of her ex-lover's rival, Julian Voss. When she inherits a share of Bramble Hollow Orchard alongside Theo Marsh — the man she abandoned twelve years ago and the estranged brother of her late benefactor, Maren — the two are legally bound to co-run the failing orchard for one season before either can sell. As Elodie secretly drafts Maren's posthumous memoirs hidden in the orchard's attic, she uncovers proof that Maren was defrauded by Voss, forcing her to choose between her career, her silence, and justice. In the climax, Elodie publishes the truth under her own name at last, sacrificing her ghostwriting career; she and Theo save the orchard together, and she finally forgives herself, choosing love in the present tense.
about_author: Freya Ashgrove is the pen name of a former orchard hand turned novelist who writes love stories about people who learn to stay. She lives near an old cider press she refuses to restore, on principle.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She finishes ghostwriting a chapter of Julian Voss's memoir, erasing every trace of herself from his voice. A solicitor's letter arrives naming her in an inheritance she never expected. Emotional beat: the ache of being unseen, and the first crack in her controlled life.

chapters.title: Bramble Hollow
chapters.summary: Elodie travels to the orchard expecting to sign away her share quickly. Instead she finds Theo Marsh — older, harder, unmistakably the man she left — hammering a 'NOT FOR SALE' sign into frozen ground. Emotional beat: shock curdling into dread as she learns the deed binds them both for one season.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He lays out the legal trap: neither can sell without the other's cooperation until harvest. They negotiate brittle rules of engagement — separate ends of the farmhouse, no questions about the past. Emotional beat: grief wearing armor, and the stubbornness of a man who never stopped loving.

chapters.title: Maren's Attic
chapters.summary: Elodie discovers a locked trunk of Maren's papers: unsent postcards, ledger pages, and the beginnings of a memoir addressed to 'the girl who owes me nothing.' She begins reading against her better judgment. Emotional beat: curiosity rekindling the writer she buried.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced to work the trees together, they fall into old rhythms — her hands remembering grafting, his remembering her. A near-accident with a ladder leaves them breathless and too close. Emotional beat: muscle memory of intimacy, resented and undeniable.

chapters.title: The Postcard That Never Went
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Among Maren's papers she finds a 1998 postcard revealing Maren once loved someone the town drove away. It mirrors her own exile from Theo's life. Emotional beat: recognition — Maren's regret is a warning shaped exactly like her future.

chapters.title: Julian Calls
chapters.summary: Voss summons Elodie to the city, pressing her for a deadline on 'his' memoir while dropping that he knew Maren — intimately, profitably. His charm has teeth. Emotional beat: Elodie realizing her employer may be entangled in the very inheritance she now holds.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Thefts
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo shows Elodie the orchard's accounts: years of payments routed through a shell company bearing Voss's initials. Maren died nearly penniless while her land quietly fed someone else's fortune. Emotional beat: shared outrage becoming the first honest thing between them.

chapters.title: What I Did in Spring
chapters.summary: Elodie confesses why she left twelve years ago: she took money to disappear after testifying — badly — against the man who ruined her father, believing she'd only made everything worse. Emotional beat: shame spoken aloud for the first time, met not with judgment but with Theo's stunned tenderness.

chapters.title: Blossom Weekend
chapters.summary: The town floods in for blossom festival; the orchard's survival depends on cider sales. Working side by side, Elodie and Theo win back skeptical neighbors, and an almost-kiss under the flowering boughs is interrupted by a phone call from Voss. Emotional beat: hope blooming faster than either can prune it.

chapters.title: The Draft Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Theo discovers Elodie's hidden manuscript — Maren's memoir — and misreads it as betrayal: she's been writing someone else's story inside his house. Their fragile truce shatters. Emotional beat: the past repeating itself, each convinced the other will always choose escape.

chapters.title: Voss Arrives
chapters.summary: Voss appears at the orchard uninvited, all generosity: he offers to buy out both shares generously and 'preserve Maren's legacy.' Elodie recognizes the offer for what it is — hush money. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into clarity; the villain smiling on her doorstep.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, alone. Reading Maren's unfinished final chapters, she confronts her own pattern: running, erasing, calling cowardice professionalism. She writes her first page ever under her own name — a letter to Maren. Emotional beat: the turning inward; forgiveness must start here.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Hollow
chapters.summary: A late frost storm threatens the entire crop. Theo and Elodie work through the night lighting smudge pots, the town rallying unasked. Drenched and exhausted at dawn, they finally say what the interruption prevented. Emotional beat: crisis burning away pretense; love admitted in the open air.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. One perfect week: harvest planning, shared meals, Theo teaching her the grafting Maren taught him. But Elodie hides the growing evidence file on Voss, terrified it will cost her the career that raised her. Emotional beat: happiness shadowed by the secret swelling beneath it.

chapters.title: The Memoir Deadline
chapters.summary: Voss demands delivery of his finished memoir in ten days — and reveals he knows she has Maren's papers, threatening to expose her ghostwriting and void her inheritance. Emotional beat: the walls closing in; every identity she wears is now a hostage.

chapters.title: Two Books, One Name
chapters.summary: Elodie makes her choice: she will finish Maren's memoir, publish it under both their names, and let Voss's book die unfinished. Theo catches her packing evidence and, instead of anger, offers to stand beside her. Emotional beat: trust rebuilt deliberately, brick by brick.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Elodie gathers the town in the cidery barn and reads Maren's final chapter aloud — the fraud laid bare, the postcards explained, the apology Maren never got to make. Voss arrives mid-reading to stop it. Emotional beat: communal witness; truth spoken where lies were signed.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Lawyers would take years Voss can outlast, so the town acts otherwise: ledgers photocopied, buyers boycott his label, a journalist runs Elodie's own bylined exposé. Voss's empire of borrowed voices collapses. Emotional beat: righteous fury channeled into collective action; belonging proven.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Climax part two. Voss comes to buy silence one last time; Theo stands between him and Elodie among the trees Maren planted. Elode refuses the check and reads him Maren's postcard aloud — the one sentence he can't buy back. He leaves. Emotional beat: the past tense finally past.

chapters.title: Harvest
chapters.summary: Resolution begins. First press of the season; the deed amended so the orchard belongs to both of them and, in spirit, to the town. Elodie signs her real name to Maren's published memoir. Emotional beat: quiet triumph; a name reclaimed is a self reclaimed.

chapters.title: Love in the Present Tense
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating POV. Winter settles over Bramble Hollow; Elodie writes her own book at the kitchen table while Theo mends fences. On the porch, a postcard arrives — from Maren, mailed before her death, arriving exactly when needed: 'Stay.' They do. Emotional beat: full-circle peace; forgiveness complete, home chosen.
